title: [bug] data loss: torn undo/redo group in the journal: SIGKILL while a multi-record tree INSERT is mid-drain restores 16384 of 262144 bytes (M); no group boundary in the journal, remainder unrecoverable after restart
description: edit-2b8 finding F1 (docs/worker-reports/edit-dataloss-s6.md in .wt/edit-dataloss-s6, test tests/dataloss_test.c torn_undo_group under --probe). Repro: 256 KiB untitled buffer, Ctrl+A, type x, Ctrl+Z, SIGKILL while e->ops[0].progress is 16384 of 262144; restart recovers 16384 bytes, expected 1 (pre-undo) or 262144 (post-undo); reproduced twice. Mechanism: replay_slice (src/editor/session.c) journals undo/redo as DELETE + a tree INSERT drained one 16 KiB record per editor_journal_staged call across turns; no group boundary; undo history cleared on restart. Same shape for replace-selection and large paste (window microseconds for small edits, several turns for large). Fix: journal group begin/end markers (or a single atomic record per logical action) so replay applies all or nothing of a group; keep the no-malloc typing path; red test is the existing probe made default.
close_reason: landed 84685d6: journal BEGIN/COMMIT action groups; uncommitted trailing group truncated on replay; dataloss_test torn_undo_group promoted to default and passes; lander made group markers not count in stats.journal_records (editor_p4_test queued_groups 2559 invariant). journal_kill_test fails identically on main 88d0ef3 (pre-existing WINDOW payload expectation)

title: [bug] P0 Astra drive 2: launch fails with exit 1 'error -103' (EDITOR_ERR_IO) and no window when a recovery journal's base file changed on disk; also hit in the ordinary profile after the first unsaved typing run, every later launch exited -103
description: Astra drive 2 (docs/reviews/astra-vs-sublime-2.md task 12, videos build/astra2/video/12-recovery-conflict-sublimite.mkv 4.333-27.529, failed-02-paced-sublimite.mkv, failed-03-nav-sublimite.mkv). title: file: one inotify instance per process (watch descriptor per file) instead of inotify_init1 per file; exhausts fs.inotify.max_user_instances (128) at ~64 open files = the CLI handoff error 8
description: Root cause of edit-jmn (Astra §9): src/file/file.c:1027 calls inotify_init1 per file; the per-user ceiling /proc/sys/fs/inotify/max_user_instances is 128 (M) and other processes hold some, so the 64th-ish open fails with EMFILE, editor_buffer_prepare returns the error and the CLI prints handoff error 8 (edit-jmn worker report, docs/worker-reports/edit-jmn.md in wt/edit-jmn-s2, has the census: available_instances=53). Fix: a single process-wide inotify instance owned by the file module (same pattern and justification as the SIGBUS service, docs/decisions/P1.7c.md §10: fixed registry, installed once, lock-free dispatch; one more sanctioned global), one watch descriptor per open file, events demultiplexed to the per-file state through the existing mailbox path; max_user_watches is 246476 (M) so watches are not the limit. Red: file_test opening 200 files with the counting of inotify instances (readlink /proc/self/fd) asserting exactly one instance; cli/ipc 200-open test from edit-jmn goes green. Keep the external-change detection semantics (the Source changed prompt) byte-identical. Update src/file/check_signal_globals.py allow-list for the new global. Label src:astra.

Wire win32_plat_present_complete to the D3D11 backend's frame statistics (docs/decisions/edit-upwq.md item 2, edit-xgcn T6); call d3d11_set_suspended on session lock/minimise as edit-xgcn §46 documents; WM_DPICHANGED RESIZE rescales font metrics (edit-upwq item 1); hot exit journal on Windows. Fix whatever integration gaps the first run shows.
acceptance_criteria: sublimite.exe opens a path, accepts typed text, saves it byte-exact (verified by a Windows test that drives the window with SendInput or posted messages and reads the file back), closes cleanly; the G1 typing-latency guard runs as a Windows test; make TARGET=win check green; Linux make check unchanged; red/green pasted; Tobias can launch it.
notes: From W2.4b (edit-177r.7, docs/worker-reports/edit-177r.7-s13.md §Found): (1) private.h session_lock / busy_source_lease are os_file on Windows but still int on Linux under #if: migrate the consumers in open.c and editor.h (editor_config.session_lock creator lease) and drop the #if; Windows rejects non-NULL legacy int creator leases with EDITOR_ERR_ARG today. (2) editor_restore_defer_file is declared locally in recovery.c: move the declaration into private.h. (3) Windows win_reparse_fixture needs the WSL interop outside the codex sandbox to read %TEMP%.

title: W2.4c editor wait set and main.c on Windows: epoll/poll/signalfd replaced by a portable wait set (epoll on Linux, a handle array into MsgWaitForMultipleObjectsEx on Windows), Windows close request and UTF-16 argv, D3D11 backend selection
description: Scope: (1) a portable editor wait set (src/editor/wait.h + wait_posix.c epoll, wait_win.c handle array) replacing every epoll_create/epoll_ctl/epoll_wait/poll in backend.c, buffers.c, editor.c, open.c, commands.c, preferences.c, fif.c, findpanel.c, font_size.c; sources register as os_wake (work_pool_wake, ipc_server_wake, file_watch_handle, config_runtime_wake which this bead adds to src/config as work_pool_wake of the runtime pool); (2) the win32 platform waits on the editor's set: plat_config gains what is needed (e.g. an array of borrowed os_wake or one wait-set handle) within MAXIMUM_WAIT_OBJECTS, X11/Wayland unchanged; (3) main.c: signalfd close request -> SetConsoleCtrlHandler + WM_CLOSE path on Windows signalling an os_wake; argv from GetCommandLineW as UTF-8; launcher/server handoff through W2.3's ipc entries; (4) editor_backend_select picks d3d11 (render_d3d11_backend_for_window with the win32 HWND) on Windows, gl/raster unchanged on Linux. Not in scope: linking sublimite.exe and running it (W2.4d), editor file-system sites (W2.4b), dependency modules (W2.4a).
acceptance_criteria: Linux make all and full make check unchanged incl. G1 typing latency and the counting-allocator test (no malloc on the typing path); a Windows wait-set test (tests/win/editor_wait_test.c) shows the win32 platform loop returning on each registered wake (work pool, ipc, file watch, close request) and on input; the loop files compile for TARGET=win; red/green pasted; decision doc records the wait-set design and the MAXIMUM_WAIT_OBJECTS bound with its derivation.

title: W1.1 src/win32 platform layer implementing x11/plat.h: window, per-monitor DPI, keyboard to XKB keysyms + UTF-8 text (AltGr, dead keys), mouse and precision wheel, focus/close/resize, clipboard, blink and repeat timers, wake-driven loop

title: W1.3 Fonts on Windows: src/font on os.h, DirectWrite fallback discovery replacing fc-match, DirectWrite rasterisation of non-ASCII and fallback glyphs into the R8 atlas
description: Scope (docs/design/windows-port.md decision 4 and §5.3 Glyphs; edit-177r.2 §9 migration rules): (1) src/font compiles for TARGET=win: its OS calls move to os.h (font_runtime's pthread_t worker -> os_thread, file reads -> os_file_*, discovery's posix_spawn/dlopen of fontconfig stays in a Linux-only discovery_posix.c); (2) discovery_win.c: IDWriteFontFallback::MapCharacters (IDWriteFactory2) on a WORK_BULK worker resolves the CJK and emoji fallback faces to local font file paths (IDWriteFontFace -> GetFiles -> local loader path, plus the face index) that the existing font_fallback machinery loads exactly as it loads fc-match's answers today; (3) dwrite rasterisation: on Windows a face loaded from a file path also gets a DirectWrite font face; font_raster_glyph/_id for non-ASCII and fallback glyphs render through IDWriteGlyphRunAnalysis (grayscale antialiasing: the single-channel texture question and the rendering mode are the worker's to settle and document; coverage lands in the same font_bitmap R8 buffer with the same placement semantics) and fall back to the stb rasteriser when DirectWrite is missing or fails. Decisions taken here (design doc §7): the baked ASCII atlas stays as it is on every platform (identical ASCII everywhere); DirectWrite renders non-ASCII and fallback glyphs only; ClearType/subpixel stays out (render.h is linear R8 coverage; a contract bead if ever wanted). Linux behaviour unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: make TARGET=win check green in rel and san with src/font in WIN_MODULES and a headless Windows test tests/win/font_dwrite_test.c: MapCharacters resolves a readable face path for a CJK scalar and for an emoji on this box; a DirectWrite-rasterised glyph and the stb-rasterised glyph of the same face and px agree in advance and bbox within a stated tolerance and in coverage sum within a stated tolerance (derivations in the report); the fallback to stb engages when DirectWrite is unavailable (injected); font_test and the other font suites pass as Windows exes; Linux make all and make check unchanged (font suites and editor suites); red/green runs pasted.

Codex sol worker (474,806 tokens (M)) + Codex sol xhigh review (10 findings) + round 2 (176,097) + root-cause round 3 (75,036): src/font on os.h; DirectWrite fallback discovery (MapCharacters → file path + face index, same mailbox protocol, user locale) and grayscale rasterisation into the R8 font_bitmap with origin translation and stb fallback; SYSTEM32 DLL search; exact placement oracle; tests/win/font_dwrite_test.c + font_dwrite_r2_test.c; font_test and font_gsub_test as Windows exes. Editor-dependent font suites wait for W2.4 by construction. Backlog edit-y63l. title: W1.2 Direct3D 11 render backend (render_backend_ops over the frozen cell grid; flip-model waitable swapchain; T5/T6; WARP fallback)
description: Scope (docs/design/windows-port.md §5.3; perf/01-perf-target.md §2.2 T5 row 'D3D11 / DXGI', §3 Present): new module src/d3d11 (d3d11.h factory render_d3d11_backend; d3d11_win.c wrapped in #if defined(_WIN32)) implementing src/render/render.h's render_backend_ops exactly as src/gl/renderer.inc does for GL: one instanced quad per cell from the frozen render_grid, R8 atlas pages as textures, strips/damage as the contract defines, DXGI flip-model swapchain with a frame-latency waitable object and maximum latency 1, T5 = D3D11_QUERY_EVENT signalled then Present returned, T6 from DXGI frame statistics, hooks delivered through the common adapter on UI; hardware device first, WARP (D3D_DRIVER_TYPE_WARP) when no hardware device exists. Decisions taken here: shaders are HLSL compiled at init on the init worker through d3dcompiler_47.dll loaded at run time (no build-time fxc, no committed bytecode); the native window reaches the backend through a module entry (render_d3d11_backend_for_window(b, hwnd)) that tests and the W1.1 platform glue call before init, so this bead does not depend on W1.0b/W1.1. Linux: the module is an empty translation unit; nothing else changes.
acceptance_criteria: A Windows test (tests/win/d3d11_test.c) creates a plain Win32 window on the desktop, renders frozen-grid fixtures (the same fixtures tests/gl_gate_test.c and tests/raster_test.c use, or a subset documented in the report) through the backend on the hardware device and on WARP, reads the back buffer back through a staging texture and compares it against the portable CPU raster kernel's output for the same grid (tolerance stated with its derivation); T5 and T6 hook timestamps arrive once per frame with the right frame id and are monotone; resize and shutdown leak nothing (D3D11 debug layer clean when available); make TARGET=win check green in rel and san; Linux make all and make check unchanged; red/green runs pasted.
close_reason: Landed e7f4509. title: W1.0b struct plat becomes backend-private; native handles and wake objects through accessors
description: Scope (docs/design/windows-port.md §5.2 cleanups, Linux-only, no behaviour change): src/x11/plat.h's struct plat keeps only portable fields (backend, width, height, focused, quit, iterations) plus an opaque backend pointer; every X11 field (conn, win, colormap, visual, depth, argb, present_ok, present_opcode, present_eid, wm_protocols, wm_delete, timer_fd, work_fd, repeat_fd, in, xi, clip, last_time, xkb_event, xkb_dev, core_wheel, xi_scroll_ms) moves to a private struct in src/x11; the Wayland state likewise. title: DECISION (Tobias): hot-exit loss window vs PRD 'no data loss on crash' (review P1.9-1 BLOCKER 1)
description: PRD s7 says 'no data loss on crash (hot exit journal)'. PLAN P1.9 specifies fdatasync every 1 s or 64 KiB on a worker with UI append cost <= 20 us, which implies a loss window of up to ~1 s / 64 KiB of edits on a power loss or kernel crash (a process crash/SIGKILL loses only what is still in the UI RAM buffers until the worker writes them: write() reaches the page cache, which survives process death). Codex review P1.9-1 BLOCKER 1 flags the mismatch and that the kill test accepts any replay in [acknowledged, issued]. Options: (a) accept the window: PRD wording becomes 'no loss on process crash beyond the last few ms; <= 1 s on power loss', kill test requires replay >= written-to-page-cache prefix; (b) write() synchronously on the UI thread per edit (page cache, ~1-5 us) so process crashes lose nothing, fdatasync stays 1 s; (c) fdatasync per edit (breaks G1). Coordinator recommends (b). Needs Tobias via the consultant.
close_reason: Tobias 15:20: option (b). Each edit is write()n synchronously to the page cache on the UI thread (bounded, a few us, counted under the 20 us append cost); fdatasync stays every 1 s / 64 KiB on the worker. PRD §7 becomes 'no data loss on process crash; at most 1 s / 64 KiB on power loss or kernel crash'. Kill test must require replay >= the written-to-page-cache prefix. Implementation bead filed.

title: P1.4 buffer kernel: 4 designs in parallel, Pareto over use cases
description: mode:par over DESIGNS (not three copies of one). Every variant implements src/piece/piece.h exactly (after P1.3b amendments) and must pass tests/piece_test.c + fuzz/piece_fuzz.c unchanged. Variants, each a Sonnet worker in variants/P1.4/<name>/ who must not look at the others: (a) bptree: piece B+ tree, SoA 384 B pooled nodes, per-node byte+newline counts, path-copy snapshots (perf section 3 design). (b) rope: balanced rope whose leaves are pieces (store, off, len) with cached counts, rebalanced on insert, snapshot = root share (xi-editor style). (c) flat: piece table as one contiguous array of pieces with a cursor cache + a sparse prefix-sum skip index rebuilt lazily; snapshot = copy the array (cheap until ~10^5 pieces). (d) hybrid: per-line gap buffers for lines shorter than 4 KiB in an array of line records, falling back to pieces for long lines and for mmapped originals; snapshot by COW of line records. Bench matrix (bench/piece_bench.c, one file shared by all variants, written FIRST by the coordinator or the first worker and frozen): rows = use cases {1 MB code file, 1 GB log (mmap), 10 GB single line (mmap, --huge corpus), dense_short 64 MB, 10^5 random edits, 10^4 cursor-typing inserts, 10^5 undo-style reinserts, 100 snapshots alive while editing (100 tabs), line_to_byte at line 10^7}; columns = {insert p50/p99, delete p50/p99, read 300-row viewport, snapshot take, byte<->line, peak memory vs G10f, first-op latency after open, .text size}. Gates from perf: G1 edit < 0.5 ms slice, G9 10^5 random edits in a 1 GB mmap < 1 s, snapshot < 1 us, G10f. Decision: Pareto front over the matrix; if one design dominates, promote it; if the front has 2+ points, an Opus best-of synthesis bead takes the dominant design and borrows the others' winning tricks. Then a Codex deep review. Record everything in docs/decisions/P1.4.md. Rules: see CLAUDE.md.

title: Typing lag: a keystroke frame is blocked behind a closing scroll window when the line-index prefix grows after the seek (editor_scroll_slice fast path requires scroll_prefix == prefix; editor_scroll_retire returns MORE while the parked worker owns the closing window; submit() refuses while editor_scroll_waiting), so the key waits for the window job to finish; root cause of editor_scroll_test:117 under load (edit-08u)
description: Found by the edit-08u Opus worker 2026-10-18 (docs/worker-reports/edit-08u-s8.md, docs/decisions/edit-08u.md), measured at load1 33.9 [AC]: 'cancellation keystroke frame not out after retries=10000: BLOCKED behind the held scroll window elapsed=359.762 ms frames=1 render_active=0 dirty=1 scroll_waiting=1 closing=1 scroll_prefix=0 built_prefix=1 scroll_revision=0 revision=1'. Sequence: a seek records scroll_prefix=0; the line index publishes prefix 1 before the typing frame is submitted; editor_scroll_slice skips its 'do not ask a typing frame to wait for replacement windows' fast path because scroll_prefix != prefix; editor_scroll_retire returns MORE while the parked worker owns the closing window, so scroll_pending stays set; submit() in editor.c refuses to submit while editor_scroll_waiting is true; the keystroke frame waits for the worker. Extra retry rounds of 0.3-0.8 s never clear it. A later redraw (caret blink) is blocked the same way. Fix candidates: relax the scroll_prefix == prefix condition in editor_scroll_slice's fast path so a typing frame never waits on a retire of a closing window, or narrow the editor_scroll_waiting guard in submit() to the case where a replacement window is actually required for the visible rows. Regression guard: tests/editor_scroll_test.c held_key() BLOCKED branch (landing with edit-08u) must pass x5 under load after the fix; G1 typing latency test in editor_test must stay green; no malloc on the typing path. Label src:editor src:view.
close_reason: Landed 8f4c7de: scrollctl fast path keyed on a certified top (SCROLL_READY, exact, extent matches) instead of scroll_prefix == prefix, so a typing frame never waits on a retiring closing window; deterministic held-window red/green; editor_scroll_test 5/5 green with 0 BLOCKED on :95 at load1 8-18 (M)[AC] (was 1 BLOCKED in 2 real runs before); editor_test san + release G1/malloc guard green

title: n95 review: a results-tab append failure (EDITOR_ERR_CAPACITY from lineidx_edit_check, PIECE_ERR_NOMEM from piece_insert) propagates from editor_fif_service through editor_step to fail() and kills the editor mid-search; a failed editor_results_open after the job is submitted appends new hits into the old results text or runs the search invisibly
description: From the Sonnet bug hunt on 87b0f5f (edit-n95), 2026-10-16 07:12. (1) src/editor/fif.c:132,172,198 return editor_results_append's rc (src/editor/input.c:462-473); editor_step (editor.c ~699-706) passes any nonzero rc to fail(e, rc), a sticky fatal error, so a pool exhausted by a large result set (4096 hits x up to 1 KB context (P) = about 4 MiB of derived text plus pieces) kills the session instead of truncating the results; f->assembled++ at fif.c:169 runs before the flush at :172, so line maps are wrong if the append errors. Fix: on append failure stop assembly, write a 'Search truncated (results buffer full)' row, clear the error, never fail(). (2) fif.c:305-321: editor_results_open can return ERR_ARG (activation busy) or CAPACITY (buffer slots full) after fif_submit; f->assembled is reset to 0, and if the old Find Results tab is active the new hits are appended into the old text (wrong text on screen); if not active the search runs invisibly. Fix: open the results buffer before submitting; on failure do not submit and show the notice. Same class as edit-601 (3): recoverable conditions must not reach fail(). Red tests: editor_test n95 variant with a tiny piece pool / capacity injection; results_open failure injection. Label src:editor.

title: qct review: lazy restore unlinks the source journal even when e->journal is NULL (nothing durable), a failure after p->retired leaves a live buffer with no BASE and an unfinished restore, and any restore failure propagates from editor_step to fail() and kills the editor
description: From the Sonnet bug hunt on f09cfa3 (edit-qct), 2026-10-16 06:30; (1) and (3) verified by the coordinator. (1) src/editor/restore.c:518-526: the flush+checkpoint is guarded by 'if (!rc && e->journal)' but the unlink of r->journal at :526 is unconditional: with the launch journal absent (open failed or disabled) the only copy of the edits is deleted. Fix: never retire the source unless the checkpoint ran and returned 0. (2) restore.c:466-518: failures after p->retired = true (:492) (calloc :476, editor_install_buffer :501, checkpoint/flush :518, editor_activate) return with state OPENING: the replacement is live under p->id with no BASE in the journal (later edits/TABS reference an id without BASE, so recovery of this launch's journal would be INVALID); restore_service skips retired p (:546) so the restore never completes. Fix: make retirement the last irreversible step; on failure keep or re-create the placeholder. (3) src/editor/editor.c:701-704: a nonzero editor_restore_service return goes to fail(e, rc), a sticky fatal error: a recoverable restore failure (NOMEM for a multi-GB journal arena, IO on BASE) kills the editor. Fix: restore failures become a notice plus the restore_fail path, never fail(). (4, crash on a hand-crafted journal only, do with the above) restore.c:476-482: the order array is sized r->count but one entry is appended per TABS id without a bound; duplicate ids overflow the heap: dedupe or size r->count + tab_count. Red tests: editor_session_test large_restore variants: journal disabled; checkpoint failure injected after retire; NOMEM injected in scan. Trial relevance: data loss and editor death on the recovery path Tobias's debris profile exercises. Label src:editor src:journal.
close_reason: Landed 78f57bc: source retired only after a successful checkpoint; retirement last with rollback (tabs_drop) on later failure; restore failures are notices, never fail(); duplicate TABS ids deduped; e601 a-d green (fixture uses forced-COPY deferral after edit-4da); journal/retire/tabs/checkpoint/session suites + release guard green (M); no-journal restore shows BASE text only -> edit-7i5

title: dz0 review: the relative repair still scans from byte 0 for the cursor when near_seed cannot prove a grapheme boundary (non-ASCII text in the 512-byte window, or the top line already spent the 4096-byte slice budget), a single very long line costs ~262k slices per key, and HOME/END/word motion/select-word still take view_command's line_at on an unindexed lazy file
description: From the Sonnet bug hunt on 5ebf309 (edit-dz0), 2026-10-16 06:25; routing claims verified by the coordinator in src/editor/input.c:1153-1158 (only LEFT/RIGHT/UP/DOWN/PAGE_* go relative) and src/view/view.c:205-218 (near_seed returns 0 when v->scanned+n+264 > VIEW_SCAN_BOUND or no adjacent ASCII pair). (1) Typing lag: view_relative_restore calls repair_begin for cursor and anchor; when near_seed fails, repair_begin starts an S_CEIL/S_FLOOR scan at byte 0 up to the cursor: a 1 GiB non-ASCII (CJK/emoji/blank CRLF runs) log, Ctrl+End, one key walks about 1 GiB on the cooperative path, the cost dz0 removed for ASCII; a top line of about 3.8 KB exhausts the slice budget and has the same effect for ASCII. The line_scanned probe does not count this scan, so dz0_key_at_end (ASCII fixture) cannot see it: extend the probe to repair_begin scans and add a non-ASCII fixture and a long-top-line fixture (red first). (2) A single 1 GiB line needs about 262,144 slices (2^30 / 4096 (P)) per typed key; accepted for jf9 motion, now on every key: state the bound or seed from the lineidx chunk nearest the cursor. title: 52o review: rotation lease can lose a recovery checkpoint (sweep unlinks a dead-owner temp whose original still matches, but journal_rotate proceeds for a failed journal, so a kill before rename loses the only complete copy) and can block the UI thread (blocking flock LOCK_SH in journal_rotate while another process's startup inventory holds LOCK_EX; editor_checkpoint runs on the UI thread)
description: From the Sonnet bug hunt on ba2beeb (edit-52o), 2026-10-16 06:16, both verified against the code by the coordinator. (1) Data loss, narrow window: journal.c journal_rotate proceeds when j->failed or j->append_failed (journal.c:736-742 region), i.e. when the checkpoint temp may hold accepted edits the damaged original never got (savectl OP_RECOVER_FINISH rotates exactly then); retire.c sweep_rotations then treats a dead-owner temp whose original generation (dev/ino/ctime) still matches as redundant and unlinks it unread. Fix direction: mark 'temp may exceed original' in the temp name (a flag character) or only unlink when the rotation began from a clean journal; otherwise set aside. Red test: rotate from a failed journal, kill before rename, relaunch: the temp must survive as a set-aside. (2) UI stall: journal.c flock(guard, LOCK_SH) blocks; recovery.c:496 journal_retire_directory in a second process holds LOCK_EX for the sweep plus inventory (reads up to JOURNAL_STARTUP_SCAN_BYTES per artifact); editor_checkpoint is called from editor.c:892 on the UI thread, so a second window launched on the same profile freezes the first window's checkpoint for the inventory duration. Fix direction: LOCK_SH|LOCK_NB returning JOURNAL_BUSY, caller retries on the next checkpoint tick; loop on EINTR. Trial relevance: Tobias launches a second window while typing in the first (typing lag), and crash during a repair rotation (data loss). Label src:journal src:editor.

title: cli_test: child hands off to another worktree's IPC primary (shared XDG_RUNTIME_DIR socket) and exits 0 before its window: cli_test:77 FAIL waited == 0 when suites run concurrently
description: After edit-63v (04d06eb) cli_test still fails intermittently under load in the coordinator's leaks-on make check: the editor child exits with status 0 before its window appears, then cli_test:77 'waited == 0' and :137 'ran == 0' fail. Expected: SKIP-with-reason or a load-tolerant wait; a child exiting 0 before mapping its window should be investigated (does the editor exit cleanly when Xvfb is slow to answer?). Rules: see CLAUDE.md.
notes: s9 root cause (coordinator): not load. The editor's IPC endpoint is a filesystem socket under XDG_RUNTIME_DIR (src/ipc/socket.c resolve: runtime dir wins over the abstract EDIT_IPC_NAMESPACE name), so when two test suites run concurrently in different worktrees (coordinator verifies, or a worker's make check beside another's), cli_test's child finds the OTHER suite's editor as primary, hands off its file and exits 0 before mapping a window: 'editor exited or stopped before window (status=0)', cli_test:77. Reproduces whenever verifies overlap (4 of ~10 runs this session), never alone. Fix options: cli_test (and every test that launches the editor) sets a private XDG_RUNTIME_DIR or EDIT_IPC_NAMESPACE per process (mkdtemp), and/or the editor refuses hand-off when the primary's display differs. Coordinator workaround now: verify.sh exports a private XDG_RUNTIME_DIR per worktree.

title: P6.4b user font selection: config key font.family / font.file, fontconfig resolution on a worker, atlas rebuild off the UI thread, swap at a frame boundary
description: Tobias 2026-10-10: DejaVu Sans Mono stays the embedded default and guaranteed fallback; add user font customisation later (he likes the Iosevka family; open to others). Scope: a config key font.family (fontconfig pattern, e.g. 'Iosevka Fixed:semibold') or font.file (path, TTC face index allowed) read by the P6.4 config loader; resolution via the existing dlopen'd fontconfig path on a work-pool worker, never on the UI thread; the face loaded with font_load_file and the ASCII atlas rasterised with stb_truetype on the worker (~95 glyphs at <= 50 us each, (E) a few ms); the new face and atlas published through a src/work mailbox and swapped in at a frame boundary; cell geometry recomputed and layout re-run once; on any failure (missing font, bad file, non-monospace advance widths) keep the embedded face and log once. Hot reload follows P6.4's inotify path. Constraints: monospace cell grid, no HarfBuzz, so no ligatures/calt: document that Iosevka Fixed/Term (one glyph per cell) are the variants to use; the advance-width check rejects proportional faces. Accept: tests (config parse, resolution failure fallback, swap happens at a frame boundary with 0 allocations input->submit before and after, proportional face rejected); editor_bench G1/G3 rows re-run once after a swap and recorded as a NEW baseline in docs/decisions/<bead>.md (cell size changes; not a regression). Deps: P6.4 (edit-v0o.7). Rules: see CLAUDE.md.
